issues.description: Buffer is an unbounded list — a crash loop or chatty job will hold every LogRecord in memory until cleanup
issues.detail: _BufferingHandler.buffer is a plain list[LogRecord] with no cap. The whole point of this path is the crash case, which is exactly when log volume spikes (tracebacks, retries, noisy third-party libs). Data dominates: choose the right structure. A bounded collections.deque(maxlen=N) is four characters more and turns this from 'maybe OOMs the worker' into 'keeps the last N records, which is all you needed anyway.'

issues.description: OTLP handler lookup by isinstance scan is fragile coupling across modules
issues.detail: _flush_early_log_buffer and _shutdown_telemetry both walk logging.getLogger().handlers looking for the first LoggingHandler instance. That's two places doing the same ad-hoc discovery, and it silently breaks if a user attaches their own OTLP LoggingHandler or if _setup_cloud_tracer ever attaches more than one. The data structure is wrong: _setup_cloud_tracer should return (or stash on the job ctx) the handler it created, and the flush/shutdown paths should operate on that explicit reference. Small composable: one place creates it, one place owns it, one place tears it down.

issues.description: Two buffer-teardown methods with overlapping responsibilities
issues.detail: _stop_log_buffering and _flush_early_log_buffer(replay=False) do the same thing. _flush_early_log_buffer(replay=True) is the only real variant. This is three entry points where one would do: _flush_early_log_buffer(replay: bool). Then init_recording's early-return path and _on_cleanup's failure path both call the same function with replay=False. Strip the duplicate.

issues.description: _on_cleanup synthesizes a RecordingOptions just to trigger handler setup — wrong shape
issues.detail: The cleanup path constructs RecordingOptions(audio=False, traces=False, logs=True, transcript=False) and calls init_recording purely as a side-effect to install the OTLP handler and flush the buffer. That's the algorithm fighting the data: init_recording is doing two jobs (configure recording, install OTLP plumbing). Split them — extract a small _ensure_otlp_log_handler() helper that both init_recording and the crash path call. Then _on_cleanup says what it means: 'install handler, replay buffer' instead of 'pretend the user asked for logs-only recording.'

issues.description: Local import of LoggingHandler/RecordingOptions inside hot-ish methods
issues.detail: from opentelemetry.sdk._logs import LoggingHandler inside _flush_early_log_buffer and from .voice.agent_session import RecordingOptions inside _on_cleanup are presumably there to dodge import cycles. That's a smell pointing at the same coupling problem above — if the OTLP handler reference were threaded explicitly, neither local import would be needed. Worth noting even if you don't act on it now.

issues.description: Makefile change drops parallelism and a test file with no explanation in the diff
issues.detail: unit-tests loses -n auto and removes tests/test_plugin_google_stt.py from the suite. Possibly correct (flaky parallel interaction, or the plugin test is broken), but it's an unrelated change folded into a crash-log PR with no comment. Either land it separately or add a one-line reason in the commit so future readers know why parallelism went away.

issues.description: test_ipc change papers over a real shape question with `if proc.pid is not None`
issues.detail: The test now guards pids.append on proc.pid not being None, and asserts a second close batch. That suggests process_closed now fires for procs that never got a pid (the new emit in _proc_spawn_task on init failure). Fine, but the test comment 'retry batch should also timeout and be killed' doesn't actually explain what changed about the lifecycle. If process_closed now means 'either initialized-then-closed or failed-to-initialize,' that's a semantic change to the event — either rename or document it on the emit site.

review.summary: The core idea is right and the shape is roughly Unix-y: buffer records in a stateless handler, replay them through OTLP when the real sink shows up, force shutdown so cleanup runs on crash. The problems are all about data ownership and structure. The buffer is unbounded (wrong data structure for a crash path — use a bounded deque). The OTLP handler is discovered twice by isinstance scan instead of being held by reference, which is the kind of coupling that breaks the moment a user adds their own handler. And there are three teardown entry points (_stop_log_buffering, _flush(replay=False), _flush(replay=True)) where one parameterized function would do. Fix the data structure and the ownership, and the algorithm collapses to about half its current size. The unrelated makefile/test changes should land in their own commit.
